plain: Steering AI by controlling the specialised chips it needs, since chips can be counted and tracked in a way that data and algorithms cannot.
eli5: You can't stop people having ideas, but you can count who has the really big ovens.
technical: Using computing hardware as a governance lever for AI: gaining visibility into who holds compute, allocating it, and enforcing rules through it. Sastry et al. (2024) argue compute suits this because it is detectable, excludable, quantifiable and made by a concentrated supply chain.
